overclaims: The cited study supports a narrower finding: arithmetic performance depends strongly on how frequent constituent terms are in training data.
checks.note: The axis (historical_observation), horizon (not_applicable) and outcome (unresolved) match the reviews. Problem 1: the rationale says performance "depends strongly" on term frequency, which is a causal claim. Per e1, the study only finds an association and explicitly declines a causal reading. Problem 2: the e1 excerpt is cut to "even 'rare' terms", which drops the point that rare terms still appear millions of times. The e2 excerpt is also a clipped fragment. The rest of the rationale and limitations are supported.
